# Results -- Study 298 (Swiftonomics) on the LYV + ^GSPC daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Eras Tour events are
hardcoded in [`data.py`](../swiftonomics/data.py) (16 events, 2022-2024). LYV and
^GSPC daily adjusted closes are from yfinance (`auto_adjust=True`), cached at
`_cache/lyv_gspc.parquet` (cache-only; network only on `fetch=True`). Match the
fingerprint below to confirm you hold the same data. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| LYV + ^GSPC daily adjusted close (yfinance) | 2021-06-01 .. 2025-05-30 | 1005 days | `01aebf313fd8` |
| Eras Tour event table | 2022-11 .. 2024-12 | 16 events | hardcoded constant |

LYV median market-model beta to ^GSPC: **1.15**. LYV pays no dividend over the
sample (price = total return); ^GSPC is price-only.

## Primary specification -- market-model event study, window [-1, +3]

For each event, OLS (alpha, beta) is fit on a 120-day estimation window ending 5
trading days before the event window; the cumulative abnormal return (CAR) is the
sum of `r_LYV - (alpha + beta*r_mkt)` over the [-1, +3]-day window.

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| events used | 16 |
| **mean CAR** | **-181.2 bps** |
| cross-event t (H0: mean = 0) | **-1.587** |
| two-sided p | **0.1334** |
| hit-rate (CAR > 0) | 43.8% |
| AAR HAC t (Newey-West) | -2.219 |

The mean abnormal return is **negative** and statistically insignificant. The
sign is the *opposite* of the Swiftonomics prediction.

## Window robustness

| Window | n | mean CAR (bps) | cross-event t | p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| [-1, +1] | 16 | -48.9 | -0.719 | 0.483 |
| **[-1, +3]** | 16 | **-181.2** | **-1.587** | **0.133** |
| [-1, +5] | 16 | -59.6 | -0.388 | 0.704 |

No window produces a positive, significant mean CAR.

## By event kind

| Subset | n | mean CAR (bps) | cross-event t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Announcements (legs, ticketing) | 6 | -402.1 | -1.476 |
| Milestones (records, film, finale) | 10 | -48.7 | -0.700 |

The "buy on the announcement" folklore is backwards: announcement events are the
**most negative** subset, dragged by the Ticketmaster fallout.

| Event | CAR (bps) |
|---|--:|
| Ticketmaster pre-sale meltdown (2022-11-15) | **-1304** |
| Ticketmaster cancels general sale (2022-11-18) | -861 |
| Eras Tour (US leg) announced (2022-11-01) | -766 |
| Concert film box-office opening (2023-10-13) | -462 |
| 2024 US/Canada dates announced (2023-08-03) | +336 |
| $1bn+ gross / Person of the Year (2023-12-06) | +246 |

The largest reactions are negative, all clustered around the late-2022 ticketing
crisis that triggered antitrust scrutiny of Live Nation.

## Placebo test

Random-date event studies of the same size (16 events, 5000 draws):

- placebo standard deviation of the mean CAR: **98.2 bps**
- placebo two-sided p-value for the observed -181 bps: **0.0672**

The observed mean CAR sits on the negative edge of the random-date cloud -- not
the positive spike Swiftonomics would predict, and not significant.

## Could you trade it? -- the costed sleeve

Long LYV (and a market-hedged variant) entered the day *after* each event
(one-trading-day execution lag), 3-day hold, one-way cost x NAV on entry and exit:

| Sleeve | gross (bps/event) | net 10bps/side | net 20bps/side |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Long LYV (raw) | -84.5 (t -0.71) | -- | -- |
| Long LYV / short ^GSPC (hedged) | -82.1 (t -0.83) | -122.1 (t -1.24) | -162.1 (t -1.64) |

Negative gross, more negative net. The short (hedge) leg would also pay borrow,
not even modeled here. There is no tradable edge.

## Positive control (synthetic)

A synthetic tape with a planted abnormal return confirms the engine fires when an
effect exists: at a planted **+300 bps** per event the cross-event t-test clears
significance (t > 2, p < 0.05) with the right sign. The real LYV tape shows the
opposite sign -- the `NONE` verdict is a statement about the market, not the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** Mean CAR -181 bps over [-1, +3], cross-event t = -1.59,
  p = 0.13, hit-rate 43.8%, placebo p = 0.07. The point estimate is *negative* and
  inside the placebo distribution; no window or subset produces a positive,
  significant effect. Single-name (LYV only) -- named on the Signal axis.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** A long-LYV-around-events sleeve loses money gross
  (-82 bps/event) and more net of costs (-122 bps at 10bps/side). No edge to
  harvest.
- **Busted -- a cultural phenomenon, not a stock signal.** The loudest Eras Tour
  event (the Ticketmaster meltdown) was a regulatory *negative* for LYV. The tour
  filled stadiums; it did not move Live Nation's stock in any tradable, detectable,
  or even correctly-signed way.
